definitions.definition: For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx. The transform extends by completion to Sobolev spaces and by distributional duality. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

definitions.type: family of Fourier Sobolev spaces and norms
definitions.definition: For real s, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2), ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials, interpreted as distributions for negative s; L2=H^0 with the normalized spatial norm. On mean-zero functions ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Time suprema use continuous representatives and derivative norms essential suprema. For sequences x, ||x||_(ell2)^2=sum_k |x(k)|^2; ell1 uses sum_k |x(k)|. Frequency projections P_{<=A}, P_{>A} retain respectively |k|<=A and |k|>A.
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k), for every real t.
P0 f=hat f(0), identified with the constant function.
Dinv=D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1): its multiplier is (i*k)^(-1) at k!=0 and zero at k=0. D^(-2)=Dinv composed with Dinv. Spatial derivatives use multiplier i*k.
For I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b, Cint_I(f,g,h)=integral_I S_(-t) P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))}dt; time-independent inputs are read as constant paths.
p_star=23/14. For an interval I of length at most one, ||f||_X(I)=||f||_(L^infty(I;L2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infty(I;H^(-p_star))).

inputs.statement: For Li-Wu's bilinear stage Stage_(n,tau)(t;f,g)=(1/2)integral_(n*tau)^t B_s(f,g)ds, for time-independent mean-zero f,g in H^sigma, sigma in (0,1], t in [n*tau,(n+1)*tau], one has ||Stage(t;f,g)||_(H^beta)<=C tau^((1+sigma-beta)/(1+sigma-beta0))||f||_(H^sigma)||g||_(H^sigma), for beta in [beta0,1+sigma]. Here beta0=2*sigma-3/2 for sigma<1/2; beta0=-1/2-epsilon with any fixed sufficiently small epsilon>0 for sigma=1/2; beta0=sigma-1 for sigma>1/2. Norms are the unnormalized source norms. The diagonal stage is Stage(t;f).

argument.text: Apply E002 with alpha=0 to arbitrary X paths on I=[a,b], 0<=a<=b, |I|<=1. This is exactly its L^infty L2 and derivative H^(-23/14) hypothesis, and any slot may carry the negative norm. For constant H^s inputs apply its time-independent clause with alpha=s in [0,1]. The source operator C is exactly Cint: e^(t partial_x^3)=S_(-t) and Fourier coefficients, projections and inverse derivatives agree. Every source L2 and H^r norm, and hence X norm, equals sqrt(2*pi) times ours. Dividing the trilinear inequalities by sqrt(2*pi) changes only their constants by 2*pi. Thus both normalized inequalities follow, also for continuous piecewise smooth paths with their weak derivatives.

H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Apply E003 with sigma=gamma, using epsilon=1/8 at gamma=1/2. Its a(sigma) equals a_gamma; all three cases give 0<=a_gamma<1. This gives ||fg||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^a_gamma). The bilinear conversion of source norms only changes the constant by sqrt(2*pi).

Fix mean-zero w in H^gamma with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, 0<tau<=1 and n>=0. Apply E004 with f=g=w, sigma=gamma. For beta=a_gamma the lower exponents beta0 are respectively 2*gamma-3/2, -1/2-1/8, gamma-1. Each a_gamma belongs to [beta0,1+gamma]. The time powers are (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma), 11/17 and (1+gamma)/2, all at least gamma. In the first case the difference from gamma has numerator gamma^2-gamma/2+1/2>0 and positive denominator 5/2-gamma; the other two comparisons are immediate in their stated ranges. Because tau<=1, this yields the tau^gamma stage bound. Apply E004 again at beta=1+gamma: the time power is zero, giving the uniform H^(1+gamma) bound. The norm conversion is again only a fixed factor, and no regularity beyond H^gamma on w has been used.
